The 2026 methodological briefings distinguish hardware-native capability,
what the acquisition SDK delivered, the observed timestamps and the grid used
by downstream analysis. The distinction matters when low-rate recordings
are interpolated to a much denser computational grid: interpolation does not
recover lost physiological information.

```{r example, eval=FALSE}
library(eyeprocess)
audit <- audit_eye_acquisition_integrity(
  time_s = c(0, .01, .02, .02, .06, .061, .07),
  valid = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE),
  device_native_rate_hz = 100,
  sdk_delivered_rate_hz = 90,
  analysis_grid_rate_hz = 500
)
audit$summary
plot_eye_acquisition_integrity(audit)
```

The plot retains the zero timestamp interval and long gap. The declared
device/SDK rates are supplied metadata; the helper does **not** verify those
against firmware, infer absent packets, repair clock drift or establish
millisecond-accurate cross-device alignment. The candidate catch-up flag is a
descriptive long-then-short interval heuristic, not a diagnosis of acquisition
software bugs.

This addition is under development; no release is implied.
